subtitle: Training and running large AI models evaporates millions of gallons of fresh water every day. Google's answer is a three-part architectural pivot: pure air cooling, closed-loop liquid systems, and routing waste heat into municipal grids. Here is the full engineering breakdown.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Google Breaks Ground in Sweden | The 9-Year Road to Horndal and What It Means for European AI Infrastructure
subtitle: After acquiring the land in 2017, clearing environmental permits in 2021, and weathering a board-level stall in early 2026, Google has officially broken ground on its first owned-and-operated data center in Sweden. The facility reframes how hyperscalers bypass Europe's power and planning gridlock.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: NASA Artemis 3 | x
subtitle: Following the Artemis II crewed lunar flyaround, NASA has locked Artemis III into a late 2027 launch window targeting a 463-kilometer low Earth orbit crewed demonstration with dual Human Landing Systems rather than a direct lunar surface attempt.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Blue Origin New Glenn Explosion | Launchpad Destruction Threatens Amazon Kuiper and NASA Lunar Architecture
subtitle: A catastrophic static fire anomaly at Cape Canaveral's LC-36 destroyed the New Glenn booster, its erector, and a primary lightning tower. All personnel are safe. The fallout reaches Amazon's internet constellation and every ULA Vulcan customer on the manifest.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Review | The Midrange Blackwell Dilemma in 2026
subtitle: The GB205 delivers real gains at 1440p and remarkable local AI throughput. But a 12GB frame buffer at $549 MSRP forces an honest question about long-term value.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Starship Flight 10 | Engineering Legacy and the V3 Transition
subtitle: Ship 37 and Booster 16 pushed the Super Heavy operating envelope to its structural limits. The telemetry from that mission is now the foundation of the V3 megarocket currently entering flight testing at Starbase.
author: Max DeLeonardis
description: SpaceX Starship Flight 10 with Ship 37 and Booster 16 exposed structural limits that directly shaped V3 megarocket design. Full engineering breakdown.

title: Keeling Curve 2026 | CO2 Hits 433.95 ppm at Mauna Loa Peak
subtitle: The annual CO2 peak at Mauna Loa Observatory hit 433.95 ppm on May 1, 2026, the highest daily reading in the 68-year record. The finalized May monthly average is expected from NOAA and Scripps in the first week of June.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Pigeon Navigation | Magnetic Compass Found in Liver, Not Brain
subtitle: A study published in Science identifies iron-accumulating liver macrophages as the primary magnetoreception hardware in homing pigeons, ending a century of debate over where birds store their internal compass.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Arctic Sea Ice Minimum 2026 | NSIDC Measured Extent and Trend Data
subtitle: NSIDC data shows Arctic sea ice extent continues its long-term decline. The 2025 summer minimum was the third-lowest on record at 4.28 million square kilometers.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Great Barrier Reef Bleaching 2026 | AIMS Survey Data and Coral Status
subtitle: The Australian Institute of Marine Science 2026 long-term monitoring survey recorded the fifth mass bleaching event in eight years. Hard coral cover on the northern reef reached a historic high before the thermal stress event.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: NASA Artemis III Mission Status | Launch Window and Crew Update 2026
subtitle: NASA has delayed the Artemis III crewed Moon landing to no earlier than mid-2027 due to SpaceX Starship HLS certification and spacesuit development timelines.

title: Ozone Layer Recovery Data 2026 | WMO Report Confirms Progress
subtitle: The World Meteorological Organization's 2026 Scientific Assessment confirms the ozone layer is on track to return to 1980 benchmark levels by 2066 over most of the globe.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: SpaceX Starship Orbital Flight Record | Reuse Milestones and 2026 Manifest
subtitle: SpaceX has now flown the Starship system nine times since the first orbital attempt in April 2023. Flight 9 in May 2026 marked the second consecutive booster catch, a milestone that validates the full rapid-reuse architecture.
author: Max DeLeonardis

title: Astronomers detect radio signals from exoplanet Beta Pictoris b
subtitle: Using the Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR), astronomers have detected coherent radio emissions directly from super-Jupiter exoplanet Beta Pictoris b, signaling the presence of a powerful planetary magnetic field.
